source.title: Agnostic Sharpness-Aware Minimization
source.authors: Van-Anh Nguyen; Q. Tran; Tuan Truong; Thanh-Toan Do; Dinh Q. Phung; Trung Le

record.file_problem: Full paper text is supplied, including appendix; no cut-off affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether its proposed optimizer changes generalization-related measurements and held-out performance across image classification, noisy-label and meta-learning settings. This is an extension of the generalization-gap topic to Agnostic-SAM and diverse training settings.
record.gate_note: Reports test accuracy comparisons between Agnostic-SAM and baseline optimizers, plus gradient similarity, Hessian eigenvalues, and loss-landscape comparisons. The latter describe measured properties but do not directly measure a train–test error gap. Results cited from prior work are not rows. Several accuracy tables do not explicitly identify whether the reported accuracy is test accuracy; the text calls it performance or accuracy.
record.test_reason: The study uses the premise that flatter minima improve generalization to develop Agnostic-SAM and reports its performance. None of V1–V8 is tested: in particular, Hessian eigenvalues and landscape plots do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking of train–test gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they present Agnostic-SAM as combining SAM with a MAML-inspired approach and claim improved generalization and robustness across classification, noisy-label and meta-learning tasks, with additional computation as a trade-off. Their claim of consistent superiority is stronger than all individual results warrant: on Omniglot 20-way 1-shot, Agnostic-SAM scores 92.66 versus Sharp-MAML's 92.89.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces Agnostic-SAM, which uses training and validation gradients to guide sharpness-aware updates; compares it with SAM and related baselines. It does not reproduce the claim versions' experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Validation mini-batch size and perturbation radii affect accuracy and training time; the authors report that beta does not significantly affect performance overall and that rho1 > rho2 performs better than rho1 < rho2 in their sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: Agnostic-SAM improves the listed ImageNet, Food101, CIFAR and ImageNet fine-tuning accuracies relative to SAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Agnostic-SAM can improve classification accuracy over SAM in the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: At 80% symmetric training-label noise, clean-test accuracy is 70.02% for Agnostic-SAM and 73.25% for Agnostic-ASAM, versus 54.47% for SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Agnostic-SAM variants improve robustness to severe training-label noise in this CIFAR-10 experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing the auxiliary gradient batch size produces accuracies from 70.58% to 71.21%, with the training batch fixed at 512.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Auxiliary gradient batch size affects Agnostic-SAM's accuracy and computational cost.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report higher training/auxiliary gradient cosine similarity for Agnostic-SAM than SAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Agnostic-SAM increases gradient alignment in the reported experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Agnostic-SAM has smaller listed Hessian eigenvalue magnitudes than SAM in both reported model–dataset pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Agnostic-SAM reaches lower measured local curvature in these experiments.

record.problems: The paper's accuracy tables do not consistently state whether the reported accuracy is on held-out test data; baseline results for the meta-learning tables are taken from cited work. Several auxiliary landscape results are presented in figures, with no extractable numerical values. Some comparisons omit the SGD baseline or report only selected settings.
record.rows_left_out: The tables contain many additional optimizer, architecture, dataset, and accuracy entries (Tables 2–7), as well as beta-sweep results in Table 8. The 60-row cap was not exceeded; rows were limited to selected entries that illustrate the main reported comparisons and distinct conditions. Table 4's flattened dataset/architecture mapping was not reconstructed because its layout does not safely associate every number with a named condition.

untested.parts: Paired random-label memorization and natural-label generalization, including chance-level held-out accuracy under random labels.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning; recovery through weight decay or switching optimizers.
Training batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, underfitting, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, association with train–test gaps at comparable training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The practical algorithm samples both nominal training and validation batches from the same training set; it does not require a separate held-out validation set. Non-testing classification rests on the experimental contrasts and measures, not merely on accuracy tables omitting the word test. ASAM's adaptive perturbations do not constitute V4's adaptive-gradient optimizer comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.
No width sweep or test-error results past interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD under the version's tuning conditions.
No large-batch versus small-batch comparison under fixed epoch budgets; batch sizes are reported but not varied as a generalization-gap test.
Measures gradient cosine similarity and Hessian eigenvalues, but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or rank train–test gaps as specified.
